title: Debug, Test and Build
introduction: Errors are normal; a repeatable debugging process turns unexpected behaviour into evidence.
learningOutcomes: Distinguish syntax, runtime and logic errors.
Use small test cases to locate a defect.
Plan a small project with requirements and acceptance checks.

activities.question: A program runs but calculates the wrong total. What kind of problem is most likely?
activities.explanation: A logic error allows the program to run but produces incorrect behaviour.

activities.question: Put this debugging process in a useful order.
activities.explanation: First reproduce and observe the defect, then make a focused change and verify it.

activities.question: A useful project requirement can be checked as pass or fail.
activities.explanation: Testable acceptance checks make it clear whether the project meets its requirements.
